He Bought a Tesla Cybertruck for $82,735, Sold It for $94,500 a Year Later
25 photos
Photo: Cars and Bids
The pre-owned Tesla Cybertruck market cooled down for a while, only to see prices go through the roof after Elon Musk announced the automaker is winding down production. The original owner of this electric pickup truck bought it last year for $82,735, drove nearly 11,000 miles, and just sold it for nearly $22,000 over sticker.
There was a time when Tesla Cybertrucks flooded the used car market with mind-blowing prices as early owners were trying to cash in. In early 2024, just months after deliveries had started, a Porsche dealership in Orlando paid $244,000 to buy a Cybertruck. Just days later, they relisted it in early March for $289,999 .
The first Cybertruck to hit a public enthusiast auction on Cars & Bids drew 510 comments and stalled at a high bid of $158,000, failing to meet the seller's reserve. From that moment on, Tesla Cybertrucks sold for anything up to $190,000, adding more drama every time and making Tesla executives raise their eyebrows in shock.
We were living in crazy times when the used car market artificially inflated the value of the Cybertruck price even by double, despite Tesla's resale clause that barred owners from selling their trucks during the first year of ownership.
Photo: Cars and Bids As far as we know, a single owner, who had listed his Cybertruck "basically everywhere," had his Tesla orders cancelled as a penalty, was blacklisted and banned from purchasing other Tesla products again. With only the Model 3 and Model Y in the lineup, there isn't really much left to buy, though.
It was by no means a lesson to others who listed their Cybertrucks on online auction platforms to get more than they paid for them. At some point, the market cooled down. In the meantime, Tesla’s inventory had gone out of control, as the automaker parked a gazillion vehicles in shopping mall parking lots or at airports without being able to sell at the pace of production.
The owner of this Cybertruck says he purchased it on November 26, 2025, which means he has just completed the first year of ownership, which means he would by no means be subject to any penalty from Tesla.
However, the automaker has so much on its mind right now that it couldn’t care less about Cybertruck owners selling their Cybertrucks. They have discontinued the model anyway, to reallocate factory space, engineering resources, and resources toward scaling its autonomous Cybercab robotaxi, and are well aware that it can no longer (actually, never could) control the used car market.
Photo: Cars and Bids Now it looks like the market is shifting again because the owner of this 2026 Tesla Cybertruck just sold it for more than he paid for it last year. His electric truck is finished in the usual stainless steel with a Star Wars-inspired partial gray vinyl wrap on the front and tailgate, over a black interior, and rides on 20-inch wheels.
The panoramic glass roof shelters a cabin with heated and ventilated seats and a 15-speaker sound system, typical of the Premium trim. The odometer reads 10,765 miles (17,325 kilometers). The truck stands on Adaptive air suspension, four-wheel steer-by-wire, and Full Self-Driving Capability (FSD), permanently attached to this vehicle and will transfer to the new owner at no extra cost, according to the original owner.
The model rolled off the production line with a dual-motor powertrain, producing 600 horsepower (608 metric horsepower) and 525 pound-feet (712 Newton meters) of torque. That is enough to make it accelerate from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.1 seconds and run the quarter mile in an estimated 12.7 seconds on its way to a top speed of 112 mph (180 kph).
The truck features the 123-kWh battery pack, which stores enough energy for a drive of up to 325 miles (523 kilometers) when it rides on the 20-inch wheels with all-season tires, before it needs to be plugged in again.
Photo: Cars and Bids The owner reports a tire fix at 9,278 miles (14,931 kilometers) earlier this year, and he has already performed a tire rotation, as recommended by the manufacturer. But why did he sell so soon? The owner jumped into the comments section to explain that he has a 2027 Model Y Premium on the way.
He went for the Model Y because he wanted "s omething a little smaller and more practical for daily use. " He bought the Cybertruck without actually needing a Cybertruck. From now on, he will do grocery shopping and road trips with the Model Y.
The EV sold with a clean Carfax report with no accidents or mileage discrepancies. For $94,500, the buyer is taking home two keys, the owner’s manuals, a windshield sunshade, the rear bed mat, adjustable hold-downs and bungee cords, along with the running boards, which are not installed.
Well, they could have bought a far cheaper Cybertruck from a dealership. Dealers sell them between $60,000 and $95,000. Recently, it has become America's fastest selling used pickup truck .
